We also respectfully disagree with the subjective assessment that a large portion of this work has
already been reported in prior studies. While previous works have indeed demonstrated various
photonic platforms, the heterogeneous integration of TMDCs with chiral quasi-bound states in the
continuum (q-BIC) metasurfaces—exhibiting both high Q-factors and maximal chirality—has not
been previously reported. We conducted a meticulous comparison between our work and previous
studies (see Figure 1b, Supplementary Fig. 27, and Table S1). To the best of our knowledge,
our heterostructured platform outperforms all state-of-the-art demonstrations across several
aspects, including the highest degree of polarization (DOP), room-temperature operation, large-
area scalability, control over the radiation pattern, and the absence of optical spin injection, which
is desirable for electro-optic transduction.
Regarding the advantages of our structure, first, it exhibits significantly higher-Q chiroptical
resonances than any previous designs aimed at enhancing valley-specific light-matter interactions
in transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs). Second, while achieving net near-field chirality
across the entire structure is intriguing, previous approaches typically require either two-step
lithography (Light Sci. Appl. 2023, 12, 250) or stringent slant etching techniques (Science 2022,
377, 1215; Nature 2023, 613, 474) to break out-of-plane mirror symmetries and attain chirality. In
contrast, our patterning procedure is much simpler, utilizing a one-step lithography process and
standard dry etching methods. We have also added the following text to emphasize the advantages
of our structure.
“Our structural design with maximal planar chirality and significantly high-Q chiroptical
resonances, in combination with simpler patterning and etching procedures, render our platform
more advantageous in enhancing valley-specific light-matter interactions in monolayer TMDCs
than other reported metasurfaces with three-dimensional chirality.22,23,25”

3b), precise control over the radiation pattern to enhance photon collection (see Figure 4), and
independence from excitation polarization (see Supplementary Fig. 23), all of which make our
structure more advantageous and appealing. Notably, the independence from excitation
polarization is crucial for the development of large-area spin-polarized electroluminescent devices.
In summary, the unprecedented properties demonstrated in our work have not been reported in
previous studies. Specifically, our platform achieves:
1. the highest DOP at room temperature among all reported heterogeneously integrated
TMDC-metasurface works;
2. chiroptical resonances with the highest Q-factors for enhancing valley-specific light–
matter interactions;
3. unprecedented scalability enabled by nonlocal chiral q-BIC modes for large-area valley-
selective emission;
4. precise control of the radiation pattern for efficient photon extraction; and
5. strong potential for electro-optical transduction due to spin-free injection.
Thus, we believe our platform represents a significant advancement toward optically addressable
valley pseudospins in monolayer TMDCs for both classical and quantum information processing
using high-Q nanophotonic architectures. Moreover, it is poised to stimulate broad interest in
leveraging high-Q chiroptical resonances for enabling chiral electro-optic transduction, single-
photon emission encoded with spin angular momentum, and spin-polarized chiral polaritons.

We also respectfully disagree with the subjective assessment that a large portion of this work has
already been reported in prior studies. While previous works have indeed demonstrated various
photonic platforms, the heterogeneous integration of TMDCs with chiral quasi-bound states in the
continuum (q-BIC) metasurfaces—exhibiting both high Q-factors and maximal chirality—has not
been previously reported. We conducted a meticulous comparison between our work and previous
studies (see Figure 1b, Supplementary Fig. 27, and Table S1). To the best of our knowledge,
our heterostructured platform outperforms all state-of-the-art demonstrations across several
aspects, including the highest degree of polarization (DOP), room-temperature operation, large-
area scalability, control over the radiation pattern, and the absence of optical spin injection, which
is desirable for electro-optic transduction.
Regarding the advantages of our structure, first, it exhibits significantly higher-Q chiroptical
resonances than any previous designs aimed at enhancing valley-specific light-matter interactions
in transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs). Second, while achieving net near-field chirality
across the entire structure is intriguing, previous approaches typically require either two-step
lithography (Light Sci. Appl. 2023, 12, 250) or stringent slant etching techniques (Science 2022,
377, 1215; Nature 2023, 613, 474) to break out-of-plane mirror symmetries and attain chirality. In
contrast, our patterning procedure is much simpler, utilizing a one-step lithography process and
standard dry etching methods. We have also added the following text to emphasize the advantages
of our structure.
“Our structural design with maximal planar chirality and significantly high-Q chiroptical
resonances, in combination with simpler patterning and etching procedures, render our platform
more advantageous in enhancing valley-specific light-matter interactions in monolayer TMDCs
than other reported metasurfaces with three-dimensional chirality.22,23,25”
Lastly, as demonstrated in our work, we achieve record-high DOP at room temperature (see Figure
3b), precise control over the radiation pattern to enhance photon collection (see Figure 4), and
independence from excitation polarization (see Supplementary Fig. 23), all of which make our
structure more advantageous and appealing. Notably, the independence from excitation
polarization is crucial for the development of large-area spin-polarized electroluminescent devices.
In summary, the unprecedented properties demonstrated in our work have not been reported in
previous studies. Specifically, our platform achieves:
1. the highest DOP at room temperature among all reported heterogeneously integrated
TMDC-metasurface works;
2. chiroptical resonances with the highest Q-factors for enhancing valley-specific light–
matter interactions;
3. unprecedented scalability enabled by nonlocal chiral q-BIC modes for large-area valley-
selective emission;
4. precise control of the radiation pattern for efficient photon extraction; and
5. strong potential for electro-optical transduction due to spin-free injection.
Thus, we believe our platform represents a significant advancement toward optically addressable
valley pseudospins in monolayer TMDCs for both classical and quantum information processing
using high-Q nanophotonic architectures. Moreover, it is poised to stimulate broad interest in
leveraging high-Q chiroptical resonances for enabling chiral electro-optic transduction, single-
photon emission encoded with spin angular momentum, and spin-polarized chiral polaritons.
